summary: Deployed a Python inventory web app (systemd service, port 8080) on node2 and node3, and configured nginx on node1 as an HTTP load balancer on port 80 round-robining across both backends. Verified firewalld/SELinux config and confirmed round-robin behavior, then executed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on all three nodes, proving changed boot IDs and full post-restart recovery of the inventory services and load-balanced routing.
actions_performed: Installed nginx on node1 via dnf
Created /opt/inventory-app/app.py (Python stdlib HTTP server) on node2 and node3 serving JSON inventory data on 0.0.0.0:8080
Created and enabled systemd unit inventory.service (Restart=always) on node2 and node3
Opened firewalld port 8080/tcp permanently on node2 and node3
Verified node1 could reach both backends over 8080
Set SELinux boolean httpd_can_network_connect=on persistently on node1 for nginx outbound proxying
Configured nginx upstream inventory_backends with both node IPs:8080 and proxy_pass in the default server block on node1
Opened firewalld http service (port 80) permanently on node1 and enabled/started nginx
Verified round-robin load balancing via repeated curl to localhost:80 and $NODE_IP:80 on node1
Captured baseline boot_id and service health on all three nodes
Restarted node1, polled until reachable, confirmed new boot_id and recovered nginx/LB
Restarted node2 while confirming node1's LB failed over to node3 during the outage, polled until reachable, confirmed new boot_id and recovered inventory.service
Restarted node3, polled until reachable, confirmed new boot_id and recovered inventory.service
Ran final 4-request round-robin check via $NODE_IP:80 confirming both backends healthy post all-node restarts

evidence.requirement: Inventory app running on node2 and node3 port 8080
evidence.summary: systemd inventory.service active on both nodes; curl localhost:8080/inventory returns JSON with correct backend hostname
firewalld permanent port 8080/tcp added and reloaded on both nodes

evidence.requirement: node1 nginx load-balances port 80 across both backends
evidence.summary: nginx config validated (nginx -t), enabled/started, and repeated curls to localhost:80 and $NODE_IP:80 alternate between node2 and node3 backend responses
Captured boot_id and active service status on node1 (nginx), node2 and node3 (inventory.service) before any restart

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: systemctl reboot issued (connection dropped=ack), boot_id changed from 583ddd53... to 87300f5a..., nginx active again and LB round-robin verified post-restart

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state, LB failover during outage
evidence.summary: systemctl reboot issued (connection dropped=ack); while down, node1's LB served node3 (proving failover/quorum preserved); boot_id changed from c2f29441... to e20cb6a9...; inventory.service active and serving again; subsequent LB check shows both node2 and node3 responding

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: systemctl reboot issued (connection dropped=ack), boot_id changed from 377b5195... to 012628fd..., inventory.service active again, final 4-request LB check via node1 shows both node2 and node3 responding correctly
